chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Yusuf al-Baghdadi narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn 'Inbasa narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Sulayman al-Malti narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) narrated to us, saying: His father Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) narrated to us from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Jealousy (or envy) is about to overtake Divine Decree.

key_terms.الْحَسَدُ: Envy or jealousy, specifically the desire for the removal of a blessing from another.
key_terms.الْقَدَرَ: Divine Decree or Destiny, the pre-ordained plan of God.
key_terms.رَسُولَ اللَّهِ: The Messenger of Allah, referring to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him).

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between envy and Divine Decree in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the Imams from Imam Ali (a.s.), underscores the potent spiritual force of envy (hasad) in Shia theology, suggesting it can accelerate or modify the manifestation of Divine Decree (qadar). It serves as a critical warning against the destructive nature of jealousy, which can disrupt the natural order of destiny, a concept often discussed in the context of the 'writing' and 'erasing' of deeds in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 35-14 Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Al-Husayn ibn Yusuf al-Baghdadi narrated that Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Anbasa quoted on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Soleiman al-Malti that Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) quotedon the authority of his father Musa ibn Ja’far (a.s.), on the authority of his father (a.s.), on the authority of his forefathers (a.s.), on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.), “God’s Prophet (S) said, ‘
Jealousy is about to overtake Divinely-Ordained Destiny.’”
